title_clean: Buying CALL vs Selling PUT - There's a HUGE Difference
summary: Foundational payoff teaching: selling a put is not buying a call. Across five scenarios (strong/moderate bullish, flat, moderate/strong bearish) the put seller profits in four and loses only beyond strike-minus-premium; the call buyer profits in one. Nifty 10,750 worked example: 212 premium vs 160 call cost.
lessons: Selling a put profits in 4 of 5 scenarios (~80%); buying a call profits in 1 of 5 (~20%) - the structural seller's edge.
Seller's cushion = premium collected: loss begins only beyond strike minus premium.
Option buying can be 'operation successful, patient dead' - the view lands and the position still loses.
Selling a call is likewise not buying a put; the asymmetry is identical on the bearish side.

title_clean: New SEBI Rules for Pledging - Collateral Margin System
summary: Explains the new pledge system: previously shares moved to the broker's pool demat, enabling misuse (Karvy, BMA Wealth) and dividend diversion; now clients pledge directly from their own demat via OTP to CDSL/NSDL; investor protection fund covers max Rs 25 lakh per client.
lessons: Pool pledging created rehypothecation risk - one client's blowup could cascade through the broker's entire pool.
Direct-to-depository pledging (OTP-based) keeps shares in the client's demat; dividends flow straight to the client's bank account.
Investor protection fund caps recovery at Rs 25 lakh - broker failure is a real tail risk; treat broker solvency as part of risk management.

title_clean: How I Turned HUGE LOSS into PROFIT by FIREFIGHTING - Infosys Trade
summary: Full firefighting case: bearish Infosys put spread + call spread faced a 780->915 (+20%) two-day run after results; added/scaled put sales (780/830/900/850, doubled 900PE) plus 1000CE sale and ~Rs 15L extra margin; net +Rs 21,826 vs -1.5L+ potential; insurance-pool and capital-gate lessons.

Size so one failed trade costs a rounding error of period profits (insurance model), not a survival threat.
